item.title: Gogol Bordello at The Warfield: Twenty Five Years In, Still Playing Like It Matters - OUT FRONT Magazine
item.description: Gogol Bordello hit The Warfield at full speed and never really let up, moving through their set like it was already in motion before anyone could catch up. With a sound that stays dense but never distant, and a voice that lands somewhere between Joe Strummer and Shane MacGowan, the band still plays with a sense of urgency that doesn’t feel manufactured. Twenty years in, it doesn’t come across like a legacy act or a routine stop. It feels like something that’s still actively unfolding.
